text:
As a VET hairdressing educator at Box Hill Institute, I have been working to design and implement an inclusive learning framework for unit SHBHCUT006 Create combine haircut structures. This units present significant pedagogical challenges, as it requires a group and learners from diverse backgrounds to master seven cutting procedures whilst integrating four fundamental haircut structures with geometric concept. To reduce cognitive load, I developed an octagon method with clock face teaching method that simplified geometric projection angles from 0 to 180 degrees.

I also integrated role playing activity and community based experiential learning to support the learner who has ADHD, ASD and social anxieties. This reflective report critically evaluates the tension between providing reasonable adjustments and upholding the non-negotiable competency standards required by Australian industry training package.

Back when I was training as a hairdresser, a one-size-fit-all approach to training was the standard. When I compare the inclusive teaching method now, I have considerable concerns. At first, I often wondered whether offering diverse teaching and reasonable adjustment might lower professional standard.

However, my teaching method and outcomes indicate that what diverse learners truly seek is purposeful learning. the core responsibility of teachers is not merely to impart knowledge, but rather to stimulate and amplify learners' intrinsic motivation, thereby facilitating a shift from initial interest to passion. This is highly consistent with John Hattie's Visible learning: teacher should see learning through learner's eyes, thereby empowering learners to become their own teacher.

In the case of Johnny demonstrated a significant leap in his learning. during the role play meeting, he proved his potential by taking on the role of a manager and achieved the teaching objectives to a high standard. Furthermore, during his voluntary haircutting work with socially vulnerable groups, he displayed a high degree of empathy and professional patience, demonstrating the ability to accurately identify and gently address the needs of clients with down syndrome and autism who struggle to express themselves due to language barrier. The thank you cards subsequently received not only serve as an endorsement of Johnny's skill but also attest to his professional integrity. This demonstration that the core education needs of diverse learners do not lie in special treatment based on pity, but rather in trust founded on deep understanding, coupled with the provision of platforms and opportunities.

Analysing this situation through the framework of Competency-Based Training (CBT) reveals a critical distinction between providing equitable support and making excessive institutional concessions. Under the Standard for Education of People with Disabilities, vocational education providers have a legal obligation to provide reasonable accommodations adjustment. Department of Employment and Workplace Relations (DEWR) also suggests this adjustment must not undermine the core inherent requirements or performance standards of the training package.

In Australian vocational education and training, learner performance is assessed against industry defined benchmarks as either Competent or Not yet competent, in my delivery of SHBHCUT006, although I actively adapted the scaffolding approach by replacing dense technical jargon with the intuitive Octagon method, the practical assessment criteria, salon safety and commercial time constraints have still remained entirely consistent for all learners. Excessive compromise often stems from a deficit model that, whilst well intentioned, is fundamentally flawed, educator lower their expectations out of sympathy, yet inadvertently foster what is known is psychology as learned helplessness.

When the education system continues to compromise on core standards in order to spare learners from feeling frustrated, it creates an extremely unreal environment. In a real hair salon, a client would not accept an asymmetrical haircut or an extended service simply because the hairdresser has an undiagnosed executive function disorder. For this reason, truly inclusive learning design must strictly distinguish between adjustments to pathways and the dilution of standards. Maintaining high expectations is not discriminatory, on the other hand, it is a fundamental ethical obligation towards learners; future employability.

To bridge the gap between reasonable adjustments and workplace survival, inclusive learning design must move beyond passive accommodation and instead focus on embedding metacognitive strategies. according to cognitive load theory, complex spatial task such as constructing haircutting structure place a significant strain on working memory. By employing the Octagon method and incorporating a dedicated 30-minute post class discussion session, I explicit encourage learners to engage in metacognitive monitoring and regulation.

For diverse leaners who are prone to frustration, developing metacognitive awareness is far more valuable than endless help and sympathy teaching there learners how to learn and adapt is more effective than simply helping them, only by equipping them with the skills to navigate the workplace will they be able to proactively adapt to the demands of the workplace when they enter the demanding social environment of the future, rather than expecting society to accommodate them. johnny is a good example to explain this. His progress is down to the fact that he found a purpose in his learning and gained confidence through practice. This demonstrates the difference between giving a man a fish and teaching him how to fish.

This reflection made me more certain that inclusive learning design is not just about compliance or political correctness, but a teaching approach that helps diverse learners slowly move toward independence in learning. For me, education should be for everyone. Every learner should have the right to learn and be supported seriously, no matter if they have disabilities, learn slower, or need different ways to understand things. As a teacher, I do not think we should only focus on learners who are easier to teach. We should try to create more pathways for learners to participate, practise, make mistakes, and gradually build their own skills and confidence.
